revision: 1. Reduce total performances to 9 (3 per stage) to meet the 8-10 requirement, increasing row height and font size for improved legibility and breathing room. 2. Maintain the three-column grid structure for the headliner by splitting it into three distinct cards aligned with their respective stages, linked by a continuous gold border/glow to preserve vertical scan flow while ensuring immediate focal dominance. 3. Enhance stage headers (SOLSTICE, AURORA, MERIDIAN) with higher contrast and weight to match the 'TIME' header, ensuring immediate column identification. 4. Introduce subtle genre-based differentiation by applying specific accent colors to genre labels (e.g., purple for Psychedelic, green for Acoustic) or varying artist name weight (bold for Rock, regular for Ambient), creating expressive rhythm without breaking the unified card template. 5. Reduce the opacity/width of vertical stage-indicator bars to make them subtle accents rather than dominant visual noise.
protected_strengths: Clear columnar alignment by stage with distinct color-coding (yellow, pink, teal).
Consistent typography hierarchy (Artist Name > Genre) and unified card style (dark rounded rectangles).
Prominent 'GET TICKETS' button and clear chronological alignment of schedule rows.
Distinct visual separation of the headliner to ensure it stands out immediately.
resolved_conflicts: Headliner prominence vs. Grid continuity: Resolved by splitting the full-width headliner banner into three stage-aligned cards linked by a continuous gold visual element, maintaining both focal dominance and vertical scan integrity.

Uniformity vs. Genre differentiation: Resolved by applying subtle, systematic accent colors to genre labels and minor weight variations to artist names, preserving the unified card template while adding expressive variety.
Information density vs. Legibility: Resolved by reducing the number of performances from 24 to 9, allowing for larger typography and breathing room without losing substantive content.
rationale: The revision prioritizes the core requirement of a scannable, coherent schedule by reducing density (Completeness) and enhancing structural clarity (Simplicity). It resolves the tension between systematic consistency (Unity) and expressive variety (Variety) by introducing subtle, rule-based genre differentiation that enhances rather than disrupts the grid. The headliner treatment balances focal distinctiveness with grid integrity, ensuring the design remains both energetic and highly legible.
